allocation.earlyStop: Every slot that cannot create an owned document is declared creates:false, so the Gate can admit a no-data abort while the run is still inside that prefix. Past that, a run that stops part way through observation ends it with the Gate's abandon transition, which reopens the recovery slots in their declared order: every document the run created is deleted and verified absent, so a frozen schedule costs this campaign no fail-closed recovery.
allocation.managementCharged: The shared Gate charges the closed management slots against the same allocation as the data schedule: five before the first data request and four after the last cleanup, thirteen seconds and one request each, all inside the published wall and recovery reserve.
allocation.openGateDefect: ambiguous or lost create responses remain owner-escalation: only a typed refusal or a complete creation proof can settle ownership, and the production lane must retain that fail-closed disposition. Production still requires the declared nx field exemption readback and the bound restore evidence; local Gate completion does not establish those production configuration obligations.
allocation.reason: One admitted allocation carries every case. Each slot declares what it can spend rather than paying the lane default: a request carrying a body reserves the transport ceiling, which the Gate's own ceiling check enforces, and a read or delete reserves the small bound that is also its timeout. The totals come from shared_gate's own charging helpers.

budgets.costNote: dataCostMicrousd is the per-request tariff for the data requests alone, which the envelope already counts: the envelope charges every request, data and management, at requestCostMicrousd on top of the fixed reserve. It is published as a breakdown, not as an additional term.

cases.boundaryUnit: utf8-bytes of the protocol resource name
cases.derivation: This boundary can only be written under the declared single-field exemption, for documents that carry the ownership marker. An automatic index entry is charged the document name and its parent document's name, and storage_name_bytes reduces to 17 plus the relative path length, so the charge does not depend on how the name is split and is smallest when the final collection and document identifiers are as long as the identifier limit allows. At a 6144-byte protocol name that floor is a name sum of 9214 bytes, so the smallest entry any document with at least one indexed field can have is 9249 bytes against a 7680-byte maximum, and the smallest entry a marker-bearing document can have is 10759. Every document this campaign owns must carry the marker for the Gate to verify and reclaim it, so no document it could own is writable at this name without the exemption. A document with no fields at all generates no automatic entries and would be writable, which is why the claim is scoped to marker-bearing documents rather than to every document. The figures here are computed by the compiler, not restated. The local shadow supervisor pins the historical index configuration and verifies its digest, so it cannot apply the exemption and these rows are pending.
expected: the boundary document is created and reads back
a read of the over-boundary name is refused the same way
cases.indexExemptionReason: Without it every document named at this boundary is refused for FS-LIMIT-INDEX-ENTRY-BYTES before the name limit is reached.

cases.boundaryUnit: bytes of one automatic index entry
cases.derivation: entry = document name bytes + parent document name bytes + field name bytes + indexed value bytes + 32, the documented single-field collection formula. The ownership marker references the document itself, so its indexed value sits at the truncation ceiling and the entry size is driven entirely by the two name terms; one byte of resource name separates the pair. No index configuration is involved.
expected: the boundary document is created and reads back
cases.localBasis: artifact shadow at 16a37e8379c289297b305c88add4a62fdbf588f8, part ALL observation rows 51 to 54
cases.semantics: One automatic single-field entry of exactly 7680 bytes is accepted and one of 7681 is refused.

cases.derivation: Under the default configuration every field carries ascending, descending and array-membership modes at collection scope, so an array contributes two ordered entries plus two membership entries for each distinct element and the ownership marker contributes two. The count moves in steps of two: 19,998 distinct elements reach exactly 40,000 and 19,999 reach 40,002. A short document name keeps every entry small enough that the entry-sum maximum stays far away. No composite index is declared or required.
expected: the boundary document is created and reads back
the over-boundary write is refused for the entry count
cases.localBasis: artifact shadow at 16a37e8379c289297b305c88add4a62fdbf588f8, part ALL observation rows 55 to 58
cases.semantics: A document generating exactly 40,000 automatic index entries is accepted and the next representable total is refused.

cases.boundaryUnit: summed bytes of a document's index entries
cases.derivation: A long document name makes each entry expensive, so the sum is reached with a few hundred array elements instead of a payload that would breach the document maximum first. A filler field whose name length is solved for carries the last bytes. The refused variant differs only in one byte of the resource name, so the sum is the only quantity that crosses its maximum; the granularity of that step is the document's entry count. No composite index is declared or required.
expected: the boundary document is created and reads back
the over-boundary write is refused for the entry sum
cases.localBasis: artifact shadow at 16a37e8379c289297b305c88add4a62fdbf588f8, part ALL observation rows 59 to 62
cases.semantics: A document whose automatic index entries sum to exactly 8,388,608 bytes is accepted; lengthening its name by one byte raises every entry by one and the sum past the maximum.

cases.boundaryUnit: logical bytes of the indexed value before truncation
cases.derivation: The catalog records this as a truncating maximum, never a refusal, and states that the truncation is what the index-entry size limits are charged on. That is exactly what this case measures: writing it as an accept/refuse pair would encode a behaviour production does not have.
expected: both documents are created and read back with their full values
a refusal of the second disproves the truncation the catalog records
cases.localBasis: artifact shadow at 16a37e8379c289297b305c88add4a62fdbf588f8, part ALL observation rows 63 to 66
cases.semantics: Both documents are sized so their one indexed entry is exactly at the entry maximum under truncation. The second carries a value twice the truncation ceiling: if the indexed representation were charged in full its entry would be 9180 bytes and the write would be refused. Accepting both, and reading both back with their values intact, is what confirms that the truncation is of the index and not of the stored value.

cleanup.probedNames: The names that exceed a request-stage identifier limit are never created and are not owned resources: the API does not consider them resources, so typed absence cannot be proven and the Gate cannot release them. If production unexpectedly accepts one, the Gate's creation-proof check refuses the proof, the campaign stops with its journal preserved, and the owned document is handed to the recovery owner.
procedure: Read each owned resource and verify its ownership marker.
Bind the exact creation version recorded by the Gate before any delete.
Delete only owned resources with a matching updateTime precondition.
Read each owned resource and require typed NOT_FOUND.
On uncertain read, marker mismatch, binding drift or incomplete receipt, stop and preserve the journal.
cleanup.recovery: No unconditional delete; unresolved resources remain assigned to the recovery owner.

collectorBinding.differenceFromLimits02: Every mutating method is gated by the write-safety predicate, not PATCH alone, because this campaign sends writes over :batchWrite. The preflight prefix length is read from the plan. A row the campaign has declared it cannot predict locally is excused from the safety predicate, though its journal integrity is still checked. collector.py is byte-for-byte unchanged, so the frozen limits-02 collector source digest still resolves.
collectorBinding.scope: REST BatchWrite per-position outcome, create-only document writes, typed readbacks and request-stage name refusals, with ownership and version bound cleanup. No configuration, index, Rules or account operation.
collectorBinding.technicalBlocker: The O8 launcher exists and drives collector_03 through the shared Gate. Production admission remains unavailable until the owner envelope, release artifact, index exemption readback, and saved receipt/restore evidence are independently bound.

comparatorBinding.addition: A per-row structural field reports status, typed error code and status, the per-item BatchWrite codes and whether the document is present, with diagnostic wording removed. It is additive and never changes the classification. It is what keeps a known wording difference from hiding the answer this campaign exists to get.
comparatorBinding.contract: The limits-02 contract: both plans are regenerated from the compiler, every ordered request including its typed body is checked, a complete response journal is required, and normalized document identity and server timestamps may differ as EXPECTED_NONDETERMINISM while everything else, message text included, is significant.

configuration.restoration: No configuration changes are permitted during the run; drift stops the campaign.

indexConfiguration.afterStateNeverCommitted: The after state is written to the tracked file only as the deploy input and is checked out again before admission; the committed file stays at the before digest, which is also what the restore deploys.
indexConfiguration.appliedBy: the executor, before the run; this campaign never mutates configuration
indexConfiguration.derivation: The three index-entry boundaries are reached under the project's default single-field configuration, in which each field carries ascending, descending and array-membership modes at collection scope: the entry-bytes boundary is tuned with the document and parent name bytes, the entry-count boundary with the number of distinct array elements, and the entry-sum boundary with both plus a filler field whose name length is solved for. No composite index is required. One exemption is required, and only for FS-LIMIT-DOCUMENT-NAME-BYTES: an index entry is charged the document name and its parent's name, and that charge is smallest when the final identifiers are as long as the identifier limit allows, so at a 6144-byte protocol name the floor is a name sum of 9214 bytes, giving a 9249-byte floor for any document with at least one indexed field and 10759 for a marker-bearing one, against a 7680-byte maximum. Every document this campaign owns carries the ownership marker, so none is writable at that name without the exemption; a document with no fields generates no entries at all and would be. The exemption names its own collection group, so it cannot reach the padding collection the index cases use.
indexConfiguration.digestNote: The after digest is the digest of conformance/firestore.indexes.json with the declared exemptions appended and the file re-serialized with two-space indent and a trailing newline. The executor must confirm the file it deploys matches it, or rebind this field to the file it actually deploys.

deploy: cd conformance && firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project fireemu-35fe6 --non-interactive
gcloud firestore operations list --project fireemu-35fe6 --format=json  # wait until no operation on the field is pending

uv run --project tools/compat-inventory --locked --python 3.12 python tools/compat-broad/fs-write-limits/limits_03_indexes.py --verify-deployed <private>/nx-field-deployed.json  # exit 0 before admission
git checkout -- conformance/firestore.indexes.json  # the after state is the deploy input, never committed; the tree must be clean for freeze and provenance
restore: gcloud firestore indexes composite list --project fireemu-35fe6 --format=json  # every listed index must be in the file: a forced deploy removes what the file does not list
cd conformance && firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes --project fireemu-35fe6 --non-interactive --force
gcloud firestore operations list --project fireemu-35fe6 --format=json  # wait until no operation on the field is pending
precondition.restoreNote: Without --force the deploy never removes an exemption the file no longer lists, so the restore must pass --force; --force also removes every composite index and override the file does not list, so the listing must be checked against the file first. The restore is verified by the field readback, not by the deploy's exit status, and bound to the production receipt.json of the run it restores -- a record cannot be produced before that run's postflight confirmed the exemption was in force, and the campaign does not close until the record is bound here.

restore.closureRequires: a verified restore record bound to the production receipt it restores

commands: uv run --project tools/compat-inventory --locked --python 3.12 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tools/compat-broad/fs-write-limits

pendingLocalImplementation.meaning: These rows state the documented production behaviour for something the local side cannot yet show, and each carries its own reason. A difference on one is evidence about the local side, not a campaign failure, and it is recorded rather than discarded. A pending row is also excused from the write-safety predicate, because a row the campaign cannot predict cannot serve as a local safety invariant.

preflight: Owner-authorized target, database and tenant are required before Gate admission.
Bind the current artifact digest after a release build; no production run may use a null artifact binding.
Verify each part's nonce is fresh and absent from every current, next and backlog campaign.
Reserve request, response, time and recovery budgets atomically through the shared reservation ledger.
Confirm the deployed index configuration equals the declared one, including the exemption, and is READY.

remaining: freeze artifact, collector and comparator bindings
obtain the owner envelope fields and tariff acceptance
deploy the declared index exemption and verify the field readback
production observation and immutable receipt through limits_03_o8.py
restore the index configuration, verify the field readback with limits_03_indexes.py --verify-restored and bind the record with package_03.py freeze --restore-record

schedule.reason: Every slot declares its own reservation and whether it can create, so the Gate charges the schedule rather than the lane default and a stop inside the non-creating prefix is admissible as no data. An observation that ends early uses the Gate's abandon transition, which reopens the recovery slots in their declared order.
